key_insight: YOR presents an open-source, low-cost mobile manipulator that combines an omnidirectional base and telescopic vertical lift to deliver a compact, versatile form factor designed for generalizable robot learning experiments.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of an affordable, reproducible, and task-flexible mobile manipulation platform optimized for research on generalization and real-world robot learning.
method: Design and open-source release of a modular hardware platform focused on omnidirectional mobility plus telescopic reach to maximize workspace in a small footprint.
Standardized interfaces and software integration to plug into learning pipelines (sim-to-real and on-robot evaluation) and enable repeatable experiments.
Cost-performance optimization and empirical validation across representative manipulation tasks to demonstrate practicality for research use.
impact: Lowers the barrier to entry for robotics and ML researchers by providing an accessible, reproducible platform for developing and evaluating generalizable manipulation algorithms, accelerating iteration and comparison across labs.
visual_elements: Exploded-view diagram of YOR hardware showing base, telescopic lift, manipulator, sensors, and modular connectors.
Cost vs. capability chart comparing YOR to common commercial manipulators (mobility, reach, payload, price).
Pipeline diagram: design → simulation/training → deployment → task evaluation (showing sim-to-real flow).
Photo montage or sequence of YOR performing example tasks (pick/place, reach up/down, navigate around obstacles).
paper_title: YOR: Your Own Mobile Manipulator for Generalizable Robotics
paper_authors: Manan H Anjaria, Mehmet Enes Erciyes, Vedant Ghatnekar, Neha Navarkar, Haritheja Etukuru
